title: CondConv-style Mirror weight synthesis
hypothesis: An input-conditioned structured Givens View over coefficients of a shared FFN basis improves held-out quality per serialized byte and synthesis compute over native linear CondConv and a parameter-matched nonlinear coefficient generator.
physical_object: K=4 shared two-layer FFN expert weight/bias bases, each mapping 12 features through width 8 to 8 outputs
mirror_coordinate: two input-generated Givens angles applied to four CondConv coefficients; all angle generator parameters are charged
controls: native linear CondConv coefficients over K=4 FFN bases
non-Mirror two-layer nonlinear coefficient generator, parameter-matched to Mirror within 10%
oracle teacher basis and coefficient function (upper reference only)
teacher: Four fixed random FFN basis functions mixed by softmax of a 12->4 tanh MLP; teacher and data seeds are recorded in results.

development.selection_metric: mean held-out normalized MSE across both development worlds; one fixed configuration, no tuning across worlds

fresh.run_only_if: Mirror improves dev MSE by >=10% versus both controls, actual bytes <=1.25x better control, compute proxy <=1.25x

storage.format: torch.save state_dict to in-memory BytesIO, exact byte length
paid_objects: all basis FFN weights and biases
Mirror angle generator weights and biases

compute.proxy: count scalar multiply-adds for coefficient generation, 2D Givens rotations, effective FFN weight synthesis, and FFN evaluation per input

success_gate: Fresh Mirror MSE >=10% lower than both native linear CondConv and parameter-matched nonlinear coefficient generator; serialized bytes and compute proxy each <=1.25x the better control.
failure_gate: Development fails either quality or byte/compute gate; do not access fresh worlds.
boundaries: Synthetic mechanism screen only; no natural language or capacity claim.
Oracle teacher reference is privileged and not a deployable control.
All methods receive identical input/output data and optimizer budget.
